context: The connected undirected graph contains vertices 0 through 6 and has 6 undirected edges: 0—1, 0—3, 1—2, 2—5, 4—5, and 5—6. The traversal starts at 0. At vertex 0, it checks neighbor 1 before 3. At vertex 5, it checks neighbor 4 before 6.
description: Solid gray lines are edges of the undirected graph. Straight dashed blue arrows show recursive calls entering unvisited neighbors. Curved dashed orange arrows show calls returning. Neither kind of arrow adds an edge to the graph. In the overview, the numbers 1 through 14 in parentheses identify 7 entries and 7 returns, including entry into the initial call and the return from the outermost call. These are event numbers, distinct from vertex numbers.

The process diagram groups the 14 events into 11 steps. Steps 1 through 8 correspond to events 1 through 8. Step 9 combines events 9 through 11, step 10 shows event 12, and step 11 combines events 13 and 14.

frames.announcement: Visit start vertex 0 and record the first result: res = [0].
frames.explanation: The process diagram uses res to record vertices in order of first visit and visited to prevent repeat visits. Braces list set members without implying an order. The initial call enters vertex 0 (event 1). Record it in res and visited before checking neighbors 1 and 3 in that order. The current call path is 0. Here res = [0] and visited = {0}. Both neighbors, 1 and 3, are unvisited.
frames.key_state: At start vertex 0, the call path is 0, res = [0], and visited = {0}.
frames.title: Visit start vertex 0

frames.announcement: Descend from 0 to 1. The result is now [0, 1].
frames.explanation: Vertex 0 has two unvisited neighbors, 1 and 3. The traversal first enters 1 recursively (event 2) and records this first visit in res and visited. Neighbor 3 must wait until the branch through 1 returns. The call path is 0→1, res = [0, 1], and visited = {0, 1}.
frames.key_state: Descend from 0 to 1. The call path is 0→1, and res = [0, 1].
frames.title: Descend from 0 to 1

frames.announcement: Descend from 1 to 2. The result is now [0, 1, 2].
frames.explanation: Skip vertex 0, a neighbor of 1 already in visited. Recursively enter unvisited neighbor 2 (event 3) and record it in res and visited. The call path is 0→1→2, res = [0, 1, 2], and visited = {0, 1, 2}.
frames.key_state: Descend from 1 to 2. The call path is 0→1→2, and res = [0, 1, 2].
frames.title: Descend from 1 to 2

frames.announcement: Descend from 2 to 5. The result is now [0, 1, 2, 5].
frames.explanation: Vertex 1, a neighbor of 2, has already been visited. Recursively enter unvisited neighbor 5 (event 4) and record it in res and visited. The call path is 0→1→2→5, res = [0, 1, 2, 5], and visited = {0, 1, 2, 5}. Vertex 5 still has two unvisited neighbors, 4 and 6.
frames.key_state: Descend from 2 to 5. The call path is 0→1→2→5, and res = [0, 1, 2, 5].
frames.title: Descend from 2 to 5

frames.announcement: Descend from 5 to 4. The result is now [0, 1, 2, 5, 4].
frames.explanation: Vertex 2, a neighbor of 5, has already been visited. Of the two unvisited neighbors, 4 and 6, the traversal first enters 4 recursively (event 5) and records it in res and visited. The call path is 0→1→2→5→4, res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4], and visited = {0, 1, 2, 4, 5}. Vertices 3 and 6 are still unvisited.
frames.key_state: Descend from 5 to 4. The call path is 0→1→2→5→4, and res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4].
frames.title: Descend from 5 to 4

frames.announcement: Return from 4 to 5. Previously visited vertices are never recorded twice, so the result stays the same.
frames.explanation: The only neighbor of 4 is 5, which has already been visited. End the call for 4 and return to 5 (event 6). Returning to 5 does not add it to res again. The call path is 0→1→2→5, res remains [0, 1, 2, 5, 4], and visited remains {0, 1, 2, 4, 5}. Neighbor 6 of vertex 5 and neighbor 3 of vertex 0 are still unvisited.
frames.key_state: Backtrack from 4 to 5. The call path is 0→1→2→5. There is no new visit, so res remains [0, 1, 2, 5, 4].
frames.title: Return from 4 to 5

frames.announcement: Descend from 5 to 6. The result is now [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6].
frames.explanation: Back at vertex 5, check its remaining unvisited neighbor, 6. Enter 6 recursively (event 7) and record it in res and visited. The call path is 0→1→2→5→6, res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6], and visited = {0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6}. Only vertex 3 remains unvisited in the graph.
frames.key_state: Descend from 5 to 6. The call path is 0→1→2→5→6, and res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6].
frames.title: Descend from 5 to 6

frames.announcement: Return from 6 to 5. There is no new visit, so the result remains [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6].
frames.explanation: The only neighbor of 6 is 5, which has already been visited. End the call for 6 and return to 5 (event 8), with no new visit. The call path is 0→1→2→5, res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6], and visited = {0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6}. All neighbors of 5, namely 2, 4, and 6, have been processed.
frames.key_state: Backtrack from 6 to 5. The call path is 0→1→2→5. All neighbors of 5 have been processed, and res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6].
frames.title: Return from 6 to 5

frames.announcement: Events 9 through 11: return from 5 through 2 and 1 to start vertex 0. The result stays the same. The remaining branch from 0 to 3 is next.
frames.explanation: All neighbors of 5, 2, and 1 have been checked. Backtrack along 5→2→1→0. In event 9, 5 returns to 2. In event 10, 2 returns to 1. In event 11, 1 returns to 0. The call path is now 0, res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6], and visited = {0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6}. The branch through neighbor 3 of start vertex 0 remains unexplored.
frames.key_state: Events 9 through 11: backtrack along 5→2→1→0 to start vertex 0. The result is res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6]. Vertex 0 still has branch 3 to explore.
frames.title: Backtrack to start vertex 0

frames.announcement: Event 12: descend from 0 to 3 and record the last vertex. The result is [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3].
frames.explanation: All calls in the branch from 0 through 1 have returned. Enter unvisited neighbor 3 (event 12) and record it in res and visited. The call path is 0→3, res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3], and visited = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. All 7 vertices have been visited, but the final calls still need to return.
frames.key_state: Event 12: descend from 0 to the last unvisited vertex, 3. The call path is 0→3, and res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3].
frames.title: Descend from 0 to 3

frames.announcement: Events 13 and 14: return from 3 to 0 and finish the outermost call, completing the depth-first traversal.
frames.explanation: The only neighbor of 3 is 0, which has already been visited. Return from 3 to 0 (event 13). All neighbors of start vertex 0 have now been processed, so the outermost call returns (event 14), completing the depth-first traversal. The call stack is empty, the final res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3], and visited = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. An orange return marker appears on start vertex 0.
frames.key_state: Events 13 and 14: the call for 3 returns to 0, then the initial call returns. All recursion has ended, and the final res = [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3].
frames.title: Finish all recursive calls

frames.announcement: Overview of the 14 entry and return events in the depth-first traversal.
frames.explanation: Enter start vertex 0 and descend through 1, 2, 5, and 4 in order (events 1 through 5). Return from 4 to 5 (event 6), then descend from 5 to 6 and return (events 7 and 8). Backtrack along 5→2→1→0 (events 9 through 11) and enter the remaining branch from 0 to 3 (event 12). Finally, return from 3 to 0 and finish the initial call (events 13 and 14). The full sequence of first visits is [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3]. The table lists the events by their numbers in the figure. Returns add no new visits.
frames.key_state: The full sequence of first visits is [0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 6, 3]. There are 7 entries and 7 returns. Backtracking adds nothing to the result.
frames.title: Depth-first traversal overview

result: Only first visits are recorded in res. Backtracking appends no vertices. Changing the order in which neighbors are checked can change the depth-first sequence. Even after all vertices have been visited, the remaining recursive calls must finish.
summary: From the start vertex, follow unvisited neighbors recursively. When there is nowhere left to go, backtrack to the previous vertex and explore its remaining branches.
title: Depth-first traversal of a graph
